result:
I’d make empathy unavoidable.

Not sentimentality. Not guilt. But a direct, felt understanding of how your words, choices, and systems land inside other people—their fear, exhaustion, hope, humiliation, relief.

Most cruelty survives because it’s abstract. People can look away from consequences when they don’t have to inhabit them. If every action carried a brief, honest echo of its effect on others, the world would become gentler not because everyone was forced to be good, but because harm would be harder to pretend didn’t exist.
